**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-15 — Reference number POC-209DEB4204-66822**
**Member:** Taylor Jennings | **Member ID:** W164265496
**Service denied:** Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
**Plan:** 'Ohana Health Plan (Commercial/ACA), State of Hawaii
**Governing policy:** 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines, effective 2026-07-01 — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), which 'Ohana Health Plan issued on 2026-08-15 under reference number POC-209DEB4204-66822. The notice states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before the requested surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the records already in the plan's possession document conservative treatment that meets the plan's own published requirement, and they also document findings that the plan's own guideline says remove the conservative-treatment requirement altogether. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I quote the plan's criteria from the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines and match each one to what is in my records.

**1. The plan's conservative-treatment requirement is met.**

The guideline states:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment that includes at least ONE of the following:"

and lists, among those options:

> "Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program"

> "Pharmacologic treatment (oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics)"

My records show both. I completed supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening for 16 weeks, from 2026-03-08 to 2026-06-28, with 24 visits completed, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief. Sixteen weeks of documented, supervised physical therapy is longer than the 12 weeks the plan's own criterion requires, and I satisfied more than one item on the list, where the guideline requires at least one.

**2. Under the plan's own note, non-operative treatment was not required in my case.**

The guideline states:

> "Complete or near-complete loss of joint space* on axillary or AP X-rays (internal rotation and/or external rotation)*"

and the accompanying note states:

> "*NOTE: In those with bone-on-bone articulation on axillary or true AP X-rays, non-operative treatment is not required"

My shoulder radiographs of 2026-07-14, taken in true AP and axillary views, show complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and a flattened glenoid. These are the exact views the plan's criterion names. So even setting aside the 16 weeks of physical therapy and 6 months of NSAIDs, the plan's own guideline states that non-operative treatment is not required for a shoulder in this condition. The denial rests on a requirement that the plan's published policy waives on these imaging findings.

The guideline also states:

> "NOTE: MRI should not be the primary imaging study to determine the extent of disease"

My disease was documented on plain radiographs, consistent with that instruction.

**3. The remaining criteria in the plan's guideline are also addressed in my records.**

> "Functional and intact rotator cuff and deltoid (adequate abduction strength); confirmed by physical examination, MRI, or CT scan"

CT confirms an intact rotator cuff, and my examination documents intact cuff strength — confirmation by both of two methods the criterion accepts.

> "Evidence of painful osteoarthritis or inflammatory, non-infectious arthritis (e.g., rheumatoid) with functional limitations such as ADLs, employment, or recreation"

> "Individual has limited function (age-appropriate activities of active daily livings (ADLs), occupational, or athletic)"

I cannot reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side.

> "Clinical correlation of individual's subjective complaints with objective exam findings and/or imaging (when applicable)"

My pain corresponds directly to objective findings: glenohumeral crepitus on examination, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, external rotation limited to 10 degrees, and the radiographic findings above.

> "Symptom onset, duration, and severity"

> "Type and duration of non-operative management modalities"

I have had 14 months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest. The type and duration of my non-operative care are set out in section 1 above, with dates and visit counts.

> "Individual does not have an active local or systemic infection"

I have no active infection.

> "Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery, and any treatable comorbidities are adequately medically managed such as diabetes, nicotine addiction, or an excessively high BMI."

My BMI is 29, I am a non-smoker, and I have no untreated substance use.

> "Individual has good oral hygiene and does not have major dental work scheduled or"

This is not addressed in the records submitted. [To be completed: confirmation of oral hygiene status and whether any major dental work is scheduled.]

**4. The two timing criteria.**

> "No cortisone injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery"

I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-12, which gave about 4 weeks of partial relief. More than 12 weeks have now passed since that date. [To be completed: scheduled or proposed surgery date, to confirm the 12-week interval in the criterion.]

> "No prior arthroscopic surgery of the shoulder within 12 weeks of surgery"

[To be completed: confirmation from my surgeon's records that I have had no prior arthroscopic surgery of this shoulder.]

**5. Request for the criteria the plan actually applied.**

Several of the guideline excerpts I have quoted end in a colon and introduce further conditions that were not reproduced in the material available to me, so the policy contains additional criteria I have not seen in full. The plan, not I, holds the complete criteria that its reviewer applied to my request. I am requesting, in writing, a copy of the specific clinical review criteria used to deny CPT 23472 in my case, including the identity of the guideline section and every element the reviewer found unmet, and the credentials of the reviewer who made the determination. I understand that my plan uses Evolent for musculoskeletal surgery review and that Evolent publishes these criteria publicly without a login, so providing them should be straightforward. If any criterion outside the language I have quoted above was the basis for this denial, I ask that it be identified specifically so that I can respond to it.

**6. What I am asking for.**

I ask that 'Ohana Health Plan overturn the denial dated 2026-08-15 and authorize total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472, as requested by Dr. Okafor. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask for a written explanation that identifies which specific criterion from the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines was not met and what documentation would satisfy it, along with information about my right to further review, including external review.

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe stated in my denial notice: the notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-11**. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also file using my state's appeal or grievance form at ambetterhealth.com by selecting Hawaii, or by calling the number on my member ID card; the address and instructions on my denial letter are the ones I am following.

Please contact me if any additional records would help. My surgeon's office can also provide the physical therapy discharge note, the radiograph and CT reports, and the operative plan on request.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

**Taylor Jennings**
